messages.subject_clean: predict linear relationships from JAGS outputs
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone!

After repeating some times a bunch of code to make linear predictions of model parameters with covariates, I have built this function that uses the samples of the posterior distribution (jagsUI) to predict mean and 95%CI:
https://github.com/ismaelvbrack/predictJAGS_func
There is also an example with the Jay abundance from the Swiss MHB extracted from session 7.9 of AHM1 book.
Hope this will be useful for others..

Cheers,
Ismael

messages.subject: Save the date: 2023 EURING Analytical Conference April 17-21, 2023
messages.subject_clean: Save the date: 2023 EURING Analytical Conference April 17-21, 2023
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

We are very pleased to announce that the 2023 EURING Analytical Conference will take place in Montpellier, France.

Since 1986, this conference has been an important forum for the exchange of information between statisticians and biologists on analytical techniques and their applications. The focus is usually on the development, understanding and integration of statistical methods for estimation and inference on animal population dynamics and demography, with data on marked individuals (via ringing/banding, DNA sequencing, GPS tags, etc). Note that contributions may also deal with unmarked individuals (e.g. occupancy or N-mixture models).

Save the date: The 2023 EURING Analytical Conference will be held on April 17-21, 2023.

Stay tuned for updates regarding a call for abstracts and workshops, registration, and more. Much of the news will be disseminated via the EURING mailing list, which you can join by sending an email to euring-l...@cornell.edu <https://mailto:eur...@cornell.edu> with EURING in the subject, and JOIN in the body. See also the official website http://www.phidot.org/euring/ (thanks to Evan Cooch!).

We look forward to welcoming you all in Montpellier.

Olivier Gimenez & Aurélien Besnard, on behalf of the local organizing committee.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dr Olivier Gimenez | senior scientist at CNRS | @oaggimenez <https://twitter.com/oaggimenez>
olivier...@cefe.cnrs.fr <https://oli...@cefe.cnrs.fr> | https://oliviergimenez.github.io/

Due to my own family/work balance, you may get emails from
me outside of normal working hours. Please do not feel any
pressure to respond outside of your own working pattern.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

messages.subject: non-convergence with simulated data (N-mix)
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

i am analyzing data from brown hare spotlight counts (~140 sites with up to three counts each in spring and autumn) where sites left and entered the monitoring scheme. Over the last 20 years, the number of sites with data decreased from about 100 to 33. Although model fit as assessed by the Chi-squared discrepancy is not perfect (mean(out1$mean$fit) / mean(out1$mean$fit.new <http://fit.new>) =~ 2) models achieve convergence (Rhat-values < 1.1) with the field data.

To assess possible influence of the decreasing site pattern on accuracy and precision of the estimates, i set up simulations mimicking the features of the field data (data gaps in sites and repetitions). To this end, i adapted the Dail-Madsen simulator from AHM2 to account for variable survey area. Although density and detection probability estimates are reasonable, all models running on these simulated data indicate convergence failure but surprisingly good fit (fit/fit.new <http://fit.new> =~ 1).

Introduction of additional variance did not result in convergence and even led to convergence failure with the field data (which is counterintuitive given overdispersion, see attached). Also running the models for more iterations did not result in convergence with the simulated data. I am aware that the pattern of the simulated data is not exactly the same as in the field data (see attached) but can this be the reason?

Any ideas why simulation models do not converge but the similar field data does?
Thanks in advance for any thoughts, (see code attached)
Tobias.

messages.subject: Latest spOccupancy package now with added multi-season functionality
messages.subject_clean: Latest spOccupancy package now with added multi-season functionality
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

in the latest version of the spOccupancy package on CRAN, Jeff Doser has added functionality for spatio-temporal occupancy models – these are the functions tPGOcc() and stPGOcc(), see the new vignette on the package website here <https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/www.jeffdoser.com/files/spoccupancy-web/articles/spacetimemodelshtml__;!!HXCxUKc!3xnejqZKRYZ6q5qmchDk8fjc1ezmx6YGCecJksP9AQBEGXFyP5dadSYVk_hg_ZWvdEBgLKYJL3ai2kJgDbXBg_0F$>. Both functions are based on the same technology as the rest of the package: Polya-Gamma data augmentation to deal with (very) large data sets and nearest-neighbour Gaussian processes (NNGPs) for dealing with spatial dependence. But now you can also model open, or multi-season, data sets. This is typically when you have data collected for more than a year for birds or perhaps for more than a week for insects. The current implementations of these models are not dynamic, but rather stratify the parameters by season and then model space- or space- and time-dependence using GPs and/or AR(1) processes. Conceptually, these new models are analogous to those in Rushing et al. (2019), Diana et al. (2021), Hepler and Erhardt (2021) and also some work by Allan Clark and Res Altwegg at UCT.

One of the cool things about the new functions is that they accept single-visit (SV) data. Spatial and temporal autocorrelation creates a sort of "fractional" replication that enables parameter estimates in occupancy models also in the SV case. (Note: This is the usual explanation for why a Dail-Madsen (or dynamic N-mixture) model often "works" with SV data.) So, provided there is sufficient spatial and/or temporal structure in your data, these new functions should enable you to model occupancy and detection separately even in the SV case. This should greatly expand the range of cases where species distribution modelling with an explicit treatment of the false-negative observation process becomes possible.

Best regards  --- Marc

______________________________________________________________

Marc Kéry

messages.subject: Node consistent with parents error
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

With apologies for posting regarding an often repeated question. I am getting the "node inconsistent with parents" error for a fairly basic multi-species occupancy model. I've created initial values, and set all site x species combinations to 1 (i.e., occupied) as per AHM1. The inconsistent node varies between attempted runs, but it is always a 0 in the data. Code is below, happy to share data if that would be useful.

Any idea what I could try to resolve this? Many thanks,
Tom

# Bundle data
test.mod.data <- list(y = species.data,
                     nsite = dim(species.data)[1],    # 124 sites
                     nrep = dim(species.data)[2],     # 2 visits
                     nspec = dim(species.data)[3],   # 71 species
                     Area = Site.area,
                     Observer = Observer.ID,
                     Jul.day = Jul.day)

# JAGS model
sink("Test_model_v1.txt")
cat("
        model {

        # Priors for species-specific effects in occupancy and detection
        for(k in 1:nspec){
          lpsi[k] ~ dnorm(mu.lpsi, tau.lpsi)
          betalpsi1[k] ~ dnorm(mu.betalpsi1, tau.betalpsi1)

          lp[k] ~ dnorm(mu.lp, tau.lp)
          alphalp1[k] ~ dnorm(mu.alphalp1, tau.alphalp1)
          alphalp2[k] ~ dnorm(mu.alphalp2, tau.alphalp2)

        } # / nspec

        # Hyperpriors for occupancy
        mu.lpsi ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
        tau.lpsi <- pow(sd.lpsi, -2)
        sd.lpsi ~ dunif(0,8)

        mu.betalpsi1 ~ dnorm(0,0.1)
        tau.betalpsi1 <- pow(sd.betalpsi1, -2)
        sd.betalpsi1 ~ dunif(0, 4)

        # Hyperpriors for detection
        mu.lp ~ dnorm(0,0.1)
        tau.lp <- pow(sd.lp, -2)
        sd.lp ~ dunif(0, 2)

        mu.alphalp1 ~ dnorm(0,0.1)
        tau.alphalp1 <- pow(sd.alphalp1, -2)
        sd.alphalp1 ~ dunif(0,1)

        mu.alphalp2 ~ dnorm(0,0.1)
        tau.alphalp2 <- pow(sd.alphalp2, -2)
        sd.alphalp2 ~ dunif(0,1)

        # Ecological model for true occurrence (process model)
        for(k in 1:nspec){
          for (i in 1:nsite) {
                logit(psi[i,k]) <- lpsi[k] +
                                   betalpsi1[k] * Area[i]

                          z[i,k] ~ dbern(psi[i,k])
          } # / nspec
        } # / nsite

        # Observation model for replicated detection/nondetection observations
        for(k in 1:nspec){
          for (i in 1:nsite){
            for(j in 1:nrep){
                      logit(p[i,j,k]) <- lp[k] +
                                alphalp1[k] * Observer[i,j] +
                                alphalp2[k] * Jul.day[i,j]

                      mu.p[i,j,k] <- z[i,k] * p[i,j,k]

                      y[i,j,k] ~ dbern(mu.p[i,j,k])
            } # / nrep
          } # / nsite
        } # / nspec

        } # / model
    ", fill = TRUE)

sink()

# Initial values, set all species at occurring
zst <- array(1, dim = c(nsite, nspec))

inits <- function() list(z = zst,
                         lpsi = rnorm(n = nspec),
                         betalpsi1 = rnorm(n = nspec),
                         #betalpsi2 = rnorm(n = nspec),
                         #betalpsi3 = rnorm(n = nspec),
                         lp = rnorm(n = nspec),
                         alphalp1 = rnorm(n = nspec),
                         alphalp2 = rnorm(n = nspec))

# Parameters to monitor
params <- c("mu.lpsi", "sd.lpsi", "mu.betalpsi1", "sd.betalpsi1", "mu.lp", "sd.lp", "mu.alphalp1", "sd.alphalp1", "mu.alphalp2", "sd.alphalp2")

# MCMC settings
ni <- 1500
nt <- 10
nb <- 500
nc <- 3

# Run JAGS
Mod.Out <- jagsUI::jags.basic(test.mod.data, inits, params1, "Test_model_v1.txt", n.chains = nc, n.thin = nt, n.iter = ni, n.burnin = nb, parallel = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: Node consistent with parents error
messages.body_plain:
Dear Tom,

that's strange, since this dreaded JAGS error usually happens in occupancy models when there is a discrepancy between the z state at initialization and the observed y data. However, in your case it seems that in addition some species have too low psi and/or too low p for the inits which JAGS chooses randomly (I believe) from the priors specified in the model. So, perhaps if you make the the uniform priors for the species heterogeneity parameters quite a bit wider this will work ? That is, for sd.betalpsi1, sd.alphalp1 and sd.alphalp2. And perhaps also for the SDs of the intercepts, especially for p.

Best regards  ---- Marc

messages.subject: Re: Node consistent with parents error
messages.body_plain:
Hey,

JAGS actually doesn’t randomly choose initial values (but this is a common misconception). From page 16 of the manual:

“ If initial values are not supplied by the user, then each parameter chooses its own initial value based on the values of its parents. The initial value is chosen to be a “typical value” from the prior distribution. The exact meaning of “typical value” depends on the distribution of the stochastic node, but is usually the mean, median, or mode.
If you rely on automatic initial value generation and are running multiple parallel chains, then the initial values will be the same in all chains.1 You are advised to set the starting values manually.
1This is undesirable behaviour and it will be changed in a future release of JAGS.”

Best wishes,

Fergus

Tom: yes, you did what I meant. Sorry it didn't help.

Fergus: thanks for reminding me of the manual.

One more idea: when I have challenging optimisation problems with maximum likelihood (e.g., fitting a dynocc model with covariates using colext() in unmarked) I often adopt a step-up strategy where I fit a simple model first and then incrementally add complexity to the model and use solutions from the last model as inits for the current model. Tom: perhaps you could try that in your case ?

Best regards  --- Marc
